techniques.description: Opens mid-panic with a physical action that triggers an involuntary trauma flashback or disorientation. Skips all geography and setup to anchor directly in visceral sensory distress.
techniques.example_beat: Kiran dunks his head under a running tap, gasping. Each splash cuts against the sound of a shattering bus window from three nights ago.

techniques.description: Opens on an intimate, mundane domestic task (peeling garlic, aligning bills, scraping rice) used by a character to avoid making eye contact and shield against an impending confrontation.
techniques.example_beat: Sumathi stands at the kitchen sink slowly descaling a fish with a dull knife. She doesn't turn around when the front latch clicks open.

techniques.description: Opens with a character in the middle of rehearsing a grand lie, adjusting their clothing, or puffing their chest in front of a mirror, completely oblivious to an observer standing right behind them.
techniques.example_beat: Surya practices his delivery action in the tea stall mirror, adjusting his sweatband. Little Bunty stands behind him holding his broken scooter mirror.

techniques.description: Opens on an ordinary routine where one physical law or sensory detail is subtly broken (silence where traffic should be, water falling upward, a clock stuck at the wrong time).
techniques.example_beat: Rahul sits at the dining table stirring his tea. The spoon scrapes against the glass tumbler, but the room produces absolute, dead vacuum silence.

techniques.description: Opens with calm, cheerful ambient sound or an absurdly mundane phone conversation while the visuals reveal severe physical danger or panic.
techniques.example_beat: A cheerful FM radio RJ announces morning weather while Vinay frantically scrubs fresh motor oil and red dirt off his car bumper with his vest.

techniques.description: Opens mid-argument over an absurdly petty financial or physical stake (twenty rupees, the last samosa, a broken chappal) being debated with grand courtroom seriousness.
techniques.example_beat: Varun slaps a crumpled twenty-rupee note on the glass counter, pointing his finger at Meera's hand hovering over the exact same pastry.

techniques.description: When caught red-handed, the character refuses to apologize. They blame external factors, switch to English technical jargon to save face, and exit muttering a petty critique.
techniques.example_beat: Caught holding the broken car key, Anji scoffs. 'Heavy tension spring defect idi. Quality control lenappudu company start cheyodhu.' He drops the broken ring and walks out.

techniques.description: Closes an emotionally heavy confrontation with zero spoken dialogue. A character performs one deliberate, mundane physical act on a household object that conveys irreversible emotional reality.
techniques.example_beat: Venkat finishes his tea in silence, walks to the third empty brass hook near the door, and hangs his own spare Splendor key before turning off the light.

techniques.description: Closes by having the straight-man character point out one tiny, unaddressed physical clue that destroys the protagonist's elaborate 10-minute cover story, leaving them frozen in silence.
techniques.example_beat: Swapna points at his collar without looking up. 'Hospital lo rescue chesav sare... mari shirt pocket lo PVR caramel popcorn bill enduku undi?' Srinu's mouth stays open.

techniques.description: Ends the scene on a wide, static frame where a small detail from the scene's beginning reappears with its meaning completely inverted or horrifying.
techniques.example_beat: The bathroom mirror reflects the entire bathroom, the flickering tube light, and the open door. It reflects everything in the room except the man standing in front of it.

techniques.description: After a fierce, petty argument, neither side concedes victory. One character takes a bitter bite or small share of the disputed item and walks away, establishing an unspoken mutual truce.
techniques.example_beat: Ananya chews the tiny burnt corner crust, staring at him. 'Next time chutney separate ga order pettu.' She swats his arm with her notebook and heads for the bus.

techniques.description: Ends on a character realizing they are not the observer, but the cause or the victim of the anomaly they spent the whole scene running away from.
techniques.example_beat: The woodcutter peers through the trees at his past self arriving by truck, slowly realizing the man hiding in the dark was him all along.

techniques.description: Ends on a physical interruption that traps the character in his lie right as he achieves a false sense of safety.
techniques.example_beat: Sridhar poses calmly. The door SQUEAKS open. He is caught in the act but pretends everything is fine.
